settings.title: Jewelry Care
settings.intro: Natural materials are beautiful because each piece is unique. With proper care, your jewelry can remain beautiful for many years.

settings.heading: Jade & Jadeite
settings.text: Jade and jadeite are durable but can still be damaged by strong impact. Avoid dropping jade jewelry onto hard surfaces. Clean gently with a soft cloth and mild soap with lukewarm water when needed. Avoid harsh chemicals, ultrasonic cleaners, and prolonged exposure to strong cleaning agents.

settings.heading: Pearls
settings.text: Pearls are organic gemstones and require gentle care. Avoid direct contact with perfume, hairspray, cosmetics, household cleaners, and other chemicals. After wearing, gently wipe pearls with a soft, clean cloth. Store pearl jewelry separately from harder gemstones and metals to prevent scratching. As a general rule: pearls should be the last thing you put on and the first thing you take off.

settings.heading: Gemstones
settings.text: Natural gemstones may vary in hardness and sensitivity. Avoid strong impact, extreme heat, harsh chemicals, and prolonged exposure to water unless the specific stone is known to tolerate it well.

settings.heading: Gold, Gold-Filled & Sterling Silver
settings.text: Avoid unnecessary contact with chemicals, chlorine, salt water, perfumes, and lotions. Sterling silver may naturally tarnish over time. This can usually be restored with a soft silver polishing cloth.

settings.heading: Storage
settings.text: Store jewelry in a dry place, preferably in a soft pouch or separate compartment. Keeping individual pieces separate can help prevent scratches, tangling, and surface wear.
